title: Catching the Wind
logline: On a windy stretch of the southern coast, kite makers fight to get a huge kite airborne, and then, for a few minutes, barely touch the line at all.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From the pleasure of watching something eat to the pleasure of watching something fly: on the southern coast in the windy season, a kite and the wish for it to be seen.

thread_out.thread: After the loud, public effort of a kite launch, wanting-to-do turns quiet and private in the southern low country: one hand polishing a stone for hours with no one watching.

requirements: An open beach or field with reliable seasonal wind
Kite makers willing to be filmed over more than one flying day
Good long-lens and wide coverage for kites at height

suggestions.name: A beach near Tangalle or Mirissa during the kite season
suggestions.why: The south coast has open beaches and a seasonal kite-flying tradition.
suggestions.season_notes: Kite-flying season is typically February to March.
suggestions.verify: No kite maker has been contacted; the season and general tradition are plausible but the specific group is unconfirmed.
